workstreams.title: Coroutine runtime, lifecycle and errors
scope: Define owned/borrowed lifetimes, coroutine-lambda capture safety, task destruction, executor affinity and reentrancy rules; examples must not require C++ coroutine internals for ordinary bots.
Provide structured task groups, cancellation propagation, bounded shutdown and a clear distinction between close, pause, reconnect and reusable-client reset.
Add setup/login/start/connect/ready/close lifecycle contracts and ready barriers, without blocking constructors or invoking the event loop in destructors.
Define exception hierarchy and context for transport, HTTP, permissions, parsing, conversion, callback and cancellation failures; preserve causes without leaking credentials.
Keep async-native execution; offload explicit blocking/CPU tasks to bounded executors and document external Asio integration and cross-thread ingress.
Define monotonic deadlines, wall-clock/calendar utilities and injected clocks for deterministic timing; prevent hidden permanent polling or one-thread-per-request designs.
Expose replaceable executors/runtime seams without forcing beginners to configure them; document ownership when users supply their own context.
acceptance: Cancellation/destruction/stop-resume races and suspended callbacks pass ASan/UBSan fixtures with no dangling captures or leaked work.
Shutdown completes within a configured bound even during a stalled network request, timer, task group or full queue.
Small subclass and function-based bots compile with documented APIs and receive actionable error contexts.

workstreams.title: HTTP engine, authentication and rate limits
scope: Separate bot authentication, OAuth2 bearer credentials, client credentials, webhook tokens, interaction tokens and unauthenticated CDN requests; do not attach bot tokens to arbitrary URLs.
Audit route normalization, major-parameter scopes, bucket discovery/merging, shared/global limits, invalid-request controls and dynamic server retry headers without hardcoded account-wide quotas.
Specify retry admission by method/idempotency and response certainty; preserve the existing refusal to blindly retry an uncertain message POST.
Bound queues, in-flight transfers, response/decompression bytes, connection pools and retained bucket state; expose admission errors and cancellation rather than unbounded growth.
Cover async DNS, TLS trust stores, proxies, IPv4/IPv6, request/connect deadlines, connection reuse, redirects and credential-safe target validation.
Add cursor/page iteration infrastructure with early cancellation, backpressure, before/after bounds and endpoint-specific semantics; retain raw HTTP response/status access.
Support per-endpoint permission/auth requirements, audit-log reasons, structured Discord error details and safe nested field-error reporting.
Keep custom transports/adapters usable; expose middleware/diagnostic hooks that cannot silently disable core authentication or rate-limit safeguards.
acceptance: Concurrent learned-bucket remapping, global/shared 429s, malformed delays, auth failures and cancellation are checked with deterministic local servers.
No request leaks credentials to a redirected/untrusted destination; request/response and queue budgets hold under sustained load.
Pagination can stop early without downloading all pages or retaining all objects; uncertain writes are never duplicated automatically.

workstreams.title: Gateway, intents, presence and protocol control
scope: Audit every documented send/receive opcode and close code, including heartbeat/resume sequencing, invalid sessions, reconnect budgets and unknown-opcode handling.
Expose presence/activity/status updates, member requests/chunks, voice-state updates, soundboard requests and channel-info requests where authorized by the current Gateway protocol.
Support current intent flags and privileged-intent limitations; preserve missing data caused by intents instead of inventing empty complete objects.
Add negotiated transport compression, bounded inflate state, fragmentation and decompression-bomb handling; treat unsupported encodings explicitly.
Separate session-ready, guild availability/chunking completion and application-ready semantics; document repeated READY/resume behavior.
Preserve raw payload access and protocol metadata while redacting secrets; allow a minimal message bot without full guild/member caches.
Coordinate identify/session-start budgets and reconnect storms with the later shard manager rather than bypassing server concurrency limits.
acceptance: Fault-injection covers dropped ACKs, reconnect/invalid-session sequences, duplicate/gapped dispatch, compression/fragments and exhausted identify budgets.
Every documented Gateway section in the upstream inventory has an explicit implementation, model or compatibility decision.
Presence/member-request APIs enforce intents and deadlines without blocking ordinary event dispatch.

workstreams.title: Models, serialization, flags, assets and utilities
scope: Define full versus partial, cached versus fetched, and missing versus explicit-null fields; keep owned snapshots and clear equality/hash/identity behavior.
Preserve unknown enum values, flag bits and new payload fields; avoid lossy narrowing of Snowflakes, permission strings and future bitfields.
Build shared User/Member/Guild/Channel/Role/Interaction partial models needed for interactions before waiting for every resource CRUD helper.
Add CDN Asset helpers for animated/static variants, format/size selection, read/save streaming and expiring attachment URLs with safe download policies.
Cover colors, UTC timestamps, timezone/calendar conversion, markdown/mention escaping, snowflake time, object references, async iteration and introspection utilities.
Audit current user metadata, primary guild, avatar decorations/collectibles/nameplates, message snapshots and application/team models against the public inventory.
Separate read-only received component models from editable builders; do not confuse outgoing file bytes with UI file-picker values.
Add schema-aware serialization tests for Unicode, optional flags, invalid encodings, integer boundaries and fields introduced/deprecated upstream.
acceptance: Payload roundtrips preserve omitted/null/unknown distinctions and large IDs; model properties never silently claim unavailable cache/intent data.
Public type/flag/utility roots in the snapshot are mapped to a typed C++ equivalent or a documented design/access decision.
Common operations need no JSON authoring, while advanced callers retain safe raw access.

workstreams.title: Typed events, state and cache policy
scope: Cover all documented event families: connection/shards, messages/reactions/polls, guilds/channels/threads/members/roles, invites/integrations, interactions, audit/AutoMod, schedules/stages, voice/soundboard and commerce.
Provide typed and raw events with consistent cached before/after semantics, including bulk deletes, uncached removals and partial update payloads.
Extend wait_for/listener APIs beyond Message/Ready/RawEvent without sacrificing predicate isolation, cancellation or ownership during mutation.
Make caches optional with entry/byte budgets, TTL/eviction, selective member/message storage and a cache-free operating mode.
Specify state ordering relative to callback invocation and cache misses, deleted references, unavailable guilds and intent-gated fields.
Bound dispatch queues and slow-listener behavior; define overload policy and ordering guarantees rather than assuming every event completes synchronously.
Document initial/repeated readiness and event replay/debug recording with explicit retention/redaction controls.
acceptance: Every upstream event-section family and discord.py event identifier has a tracked handler/model decision; raw ingress alone does not count as typed coverage.
Cache-free, evicted, unavailable and partial-update fixtures produce documented values and preserve callback lifetimes.
Long-running dispatch/cancellation tests remain within configured state and queue budgets.

workstreams.title: Complete prefix-command framework
scope: Add command groups/subcommands, command walking/lookup/removal, enabled state, qualified names, aliases and case-insensitive policy.
Support static/multiple/callable prefixes, mention prefixes, per-guild resolution and explicit whitespace/empty-prefix semantics.
Extend converters to domain models/mentions, choices/literals/unions, greedy/variadic arguments, ranges, timestamps, attachments and named flags with clear ambiguity rules.
Provide parameter metadata/defaults, custom converter/transformer injection, clean-content behavior and readable compile/runtime diagnostics.
Add owner/role/permission/NSFW checks, composite/check-once/global/Cog checks, before/after invocation hooks and documented error-handler precedence.
Add configurable/dynamic cooldown policies, max concurrency and queue/cancellation behavior; keep aliases from bypassing admission.
Expose invoke/reinvoke/get_context/process_commands hooks and hybrid-command foundations while retaining default command processing when on_message is overridden.
Bound parsing/conversion work and avoid implicit unbounded fetches during model conversion; preserve command identity on every failure path.
acceptance: Every public command/converter/check/error family in the inventory has a mapping; argument quoting, conversion order and callback ownership remain regression-tested.
Nested/aliased/disabled commands and asynchronous checks interact correctly with cancellation, cooldowns and error routing.
Common typed commands require short owning callbacks and actionable failures rather than template backtraces alone.

workstreams.title: Automatic and fully replaceable help
scope: Design a HelpCommand/provider abstraction with replaceable rendering, sending, filtering and error hooks; avoid a fixed non-virtual text formatter as the only extension point.

Provide automatic default registration in the chosen new Bot API with explicit disable, rename and replacement controls; migrate current opt-in add_help_command users without duplicate-registration breakage.
Offer default/minimal formatters, generated signatures, argument descriptions, aliases, command groups and Cog categories.
Support localization, custom embeds and safe text/embed pagination; allow applications to implement their own UI renderer after the component layer exists.
Define visibility/check/cooldown handling so help neither leaks private commands nor consumes command admission unexpectedly.
Integrate prefix, hybrid, slash and context-menu discovery where registered, distinguishing remotely synchronized commands from local-only definitions.
acceptance: Examples cover zero-configuration default help, disabled help, renamed help and a custom class-based formatter without copying internal command code.
Large/Unicode help stays within the current payload limits; permission filtering does not execute destructive or admission-consuming checks.
Replacing/removing help during an in-flight callback preserves ownership and error isolation.

workstreams.title: Cogs, extensions and reload lifecycle
scope: Add Cog load/unload/setup hooks, listeners, checks and command error handling with deterministic order and rollback on failure.
Support command groups and application-command GroupCog-like ownership after the CommandTree layer is available.
Add extension setup/teardown, dependency ordering, registry introspection and transactional load/unload/reload behavior.
Specify managed background-task, listener, View and modal cleanup; keep callbacks already executing alive during unload/reload.
Use source registration/factories as the portable default; treat shared-library hot reload as an explicit ABI/lifetime design rather than blindly copying Python module semantics.
Expose name/qualified-name/documentation metadata and safe duplicate/conflict behavior across prefix and application commands.
acceptance: Failed setup/reload leaves the previous working registry intact; no callbacks execute through unloaded code.
Subclass examples demonstrate reusable Cogs containing commands, listeners, tasks and later UI/application commands.
Concurrent unload, cancellation and task completion have bounded, documented cleanup behavior.

workstreams.title: Managed background loops and scheduling
scope: Provide loop/start/stop/cancel/restart APIs with before/after/error hooks, running/failed state, task access and iteration counters.
Support fixed intervals and timezone-aware calendar schedules, interval changes and well-defined daylight-saving/clock-change behavior.
Add bounded reconnect/backoff and configurable retryable exception classes without swallowing permanent application errors.
Coordinate readiness waits, overlap prevention, missed ticks, catch-up policy and shutdown/Cog cancellation.
Separate clean stop-after-current-iteration from immediate cancellation and define cancellation during startup/after-loop hooks.
acceptance: Injected-clock tests cover reconnect, stop/cancel/restart races, scheduling changes, DST and shutdown while a callback is suspended.
Loop ownership is released after Cog unload; no hidden worker/thread survives client destruction.
Examples match the practical tasks.loop use cases with clear coroutine errors.

workstreams.title: Interaction ingress and response lifecycle
scope: Parse every current interaction type, resolved values, locales, authorizing owners/install contexts, permissions, entitlements and partial DM/guild data.
Support Gateway ingress and an optional framework-neutral HTTP adapter with PING handling and verification of the original signed body and timestamp.
Implement initial reply, defer, message update/deferred update, autocomplete, modal opening and supported callback-response metadata with an explicit one-initial-response state machine.
Enforce the current initial-response deadline and token lifetime from the reviewed specification; define expired/acknowledged errors and safe concurrent response attempts.
Provide original-response fetch/edit/delete and followup send/edit/delete, ephemeral policy, attachment retention and typed callback results.
Keep interaction/webhook credentials out of repr/logs/URLs exposed to diagnostics; bound signed payloads, deduplicate retried ingress and handle out-of-order HTTP delivery appropriately.
Keep automatic defer configurable and race-safe; do not double-respond or blindly retry an uncertain initial callback.
Track activity-launch/entry-point callback variants with explicit platform-access requirements rather than promising unsupported application modes.
acceptance: Signed HTTP fixtures reject tampered bodies/signatures and support verification without altering the body before validation.
Deadline expiry, concurrent initial replies, defer/followup/edit sequences and ephemeral/component payloads pass state-machine fixtures.
A minimal slash bot and HTTP-only interaction example work without full guild/member caches or raw JSON construction.

workstreams.title: CommandTree, slash, context menus and hybrid commands
scope: Provide a Bot-integrated CommandTree with typed slash commands, user/message context menus, groups/subcommands and stable local lookup/removal.
Implement global/guild command CRUD, diff/preview sync, opt-in destructive deletion, stable IDs and explicit remote/local reconciliation.
Support parameter naming/descriptions, required/default values, choices, autocomplete, min/max values/lengths, channel constraints, attachments and current timestamp transforms.
Support user/guild installs, interaction contexts, default permissions, age restriction, localization/translation and supported entry-point command modes.
Implement tree/global/Cog/local checks, converters/transformers, cooldowns and error/completion hooks with asynchronous callback ownership.
Add hybrid prefix/slash definitions and document unsupported argument shapes instead of silently changing conversion semantics.
Handle command-registration budgets, stale remote signatures, partial sync failures and permissions endpoints requiring OAuth2 grants.
acceptance: Contract tests cover slash/user/message/group/autocomplete payloads and synchronization without deleting unrelated application commands.
Bot.tree-style examples, Cog application commands and hybrid commands use a coherent owning C++ interface.
DM/user-install and guild-installed invocations resolve incomplete model data and permissions consistently.

workstreams.title: Legacy components, buttons, selects and View
scope: Implement read models and builders for ActionRow and every documented button style, including link/premium behavior and non-callback controls where applicable.
Implement String/User/Role/Mentionable/Channel Select menus, options, defaults, placeholders, required/min/max values and typed resolved selections.
Provide class/callback View APIs with custom IDs, interaction checks, errors, timeout, stop/wait and disabled/replaced controls.
Route interactions by message/custom ID with collision handling and state ownership; support message edit, deletion and fetched-component reconstruction.
Support persistent and dynamic item registration with explicit durable state/versioning expectations and restart recovery hooks.
Validate current per-container and nesting rules, UTF-8 limits and numeric component IDs separately from custom IDs.
acceptance: Every current button/select category has create/edit/parse and callback fixtures, including controls that do not generate callbacks.
Timeout, deletion, concurrent clicks, duplicate IDs and View removal during suspended handlers are deterministic and leak-free.
An ordinary paginator/confirmation/role-selection example requires no raw REST/JSON or manual callback table.

workstreams.title: Components V2 and LayoutView
scope: Implement Container, Section, TextDisplay, Thumbnail, MediaGallery, File and Separator with compatible ActionRows/buttons/selects and read-only incoming counterparts.
Provide nested LayoutView-style class/builders, traversal/counting and fluent or named-field construction with owning media/attachment references.
Apply IS_COMPONENTS_V2 correctly on send/edit and enforce the platform's irreversible flag transition and content/embed/poll/sticker incompatibilities.
Handle section accessories, file/gallery/spoiler metadata, media descriptions and allowed nesting/count/size limits from the current reference rather than guessed fixed layouts.
Expose uploaded attachments through the appropriate display components and preserve attachment retention/allowed-mention policy while editing layouts.
Support reconstructing/editing received layouts and safe conversion boundaries between legacy View and V2 layouts.
acceptance: The component-type inventory has explicit coverage for all current message V2 types and their placement/validation rules.
Prefix and slash examples send, fetch, edit and paginate a real modeled layout; embeds are never presented as a substitute for V2 support.
Invalid nested layouts, incompatible payload fields and attempts to clear the V2 flag fail before network I/O with useful errors.

workstreams.title: Modern modals and every current modal control
scope: Provide Modal subclasses/callbacks with submit/error/timeout/stop lifecycle and safe ownership after the originating View/Cog is removed.
Implement Label/TextDisplay modal layout, TextInput and every currently permitted select type with the current placement/required/default rules.
Implement modal FileUpload/file-type filtering, RadioGroup, CheckboxGroup and Checkbox with distinct types from outgoing message-file bytes.
Parse submitted values and resolved attachments/users/roles/channels without requiring a full cache; distinguish absent, empty, false and invalid values.
Validate every allowed parent/child placement and unsupported legacy/deprecated schema, rather than treating all V2 message elements as modal elements.
Coordinate show-modal versus initial-response state, nested interaction restrictions, expiration and duplicate/late submissions.
acceptance: All component types marked Modal in the upstream inventory have parsing, serialization, validation and callback tests.
Examples demonstrate a modern multi-control form and file-picker submission, including invalid, cancelled and timed-out forms.
Submitted external files are not downloaded automatically; access and streaming limits are explicit.

workstreams.title: Roles, permissions and effective access
scope: Implement current permission flags, role models/tags/icons/managed status, role CRUD/order and member counts where supported.
Implement channel/member/role overwrite CRUD and effective-permission resolution for owners, administrators, hierarchy, timeouts, threads and partial objects.
Support newer server-side member/role permission endpoints without confusing their results with locally computed incomplete-cache permissions.
Preserve unknown future permission bits and expose raw bitfields without silent narrowing or treating unknown flags as granted.
Reuse explicit permission/role checks in commands, interactions and UI; distinguish missing bot permissions from missing invoking-user permissions.
acceptance: Table-driven permission fixtures cover hierarchy, overwrite precedence, administrator/owner behavior, timeouts and thread inheritance.
Unknown bits and incomplete state are preserved or produce explicit indeterminate/fetch-required results.
Role mutation and checks report the applicable API permission/hierarchy failure without a speculative client-side success claim.

workstreams.title: Users, members, DMs and moderation
scope: Implement User/ClientUser/Member fetch/edit, profiles/avatars/banners/primary-guild metadata and explicit partial-member semantics.
Support bot-authorized DM creation/sends, leave-guild, current user updates and typing/history conveniences with correct blocked/permission errors.
Add member list/search/chunking, role assignment, nicknames, timeouts, kick/ban/unban/bulk bans and prune workflows with audit reasons.
Respect privileged intents, hierarchy, pagination and rate limits; return partial results for bulk operations rather than hiding per-target failures.
Keep OAuth-only user connections/group-DM recipient/account-link operations behind the separate OAuth2 capability path.
acceptance: Member intents/cache absence, departed users, blocked DMs, hierarchy failures and bulk partial failures have explicit fixtures.
User/member converters and context menus work from interaction-resolved data without an automatic complete-member download.
Destructive operations require explicit application calls and expose their audit/error results.

workstreams.title: Guilds, onboarding, integrations, invites and templates
scope: Implement Guild/preview fetch/edit, features/limits/assets, availability, bans/invites/integrations and supported administrative configuration.
Cover welcome screens, onboarding prompts/options/default channels, widgets, vanity invites, incident actions and current safety settings.
Implement templates, invite fetch/create/delete/resolve, scheduled-event invite associations and permission/audit requirements.
Model integration accounts/applications, partial/deleted integrations and bot/application-specific resource limitations.
Keep creation/deletion and OAuth-authorized actions constrained to currently supported bot/app capabilities; do not recreate removed API behavior merely because older examples used it.
acceptance: Every Guild/Invite/Template resource endpoint in the snapshot is assigned a wrapper, access-gated decision or explicit deprecated mapping.
Onboarding, unavailable guilds, optional premium features and partial integration/invite targets roundtrip correctly.
Guild edits and destructive operations preserve audit reasons and report permission/access restrictions.

workstreams.title: All channel types, forums, media and threads
scope: Implement text/announcement/category/voice/stage/forum/media/DM/partial channel models and supported CRUD, ordering, permissions and typing.
Add thread creation from messages or standalone/forum/media posts, join/leave/member management and active/archived/private pagination.
Model forum/media tags, post defaults, applied tags, archive/lock/invite/slowmode settings and ownership/access behavior.
Support announcement following/crossposting and voice channel status where documented; distinguish text-in-voice from audio transport.
Track group-DM recipient operations as OAuth/access-gated rather than pretending bot-token support.
Integrate channel/member/role permission endpoints, uncached IDs and converters with explicit fetch policy.
acceptance: Every channel/thread operation in the upstream inventory has a planned API/access decision and paginated response fixture.
Archived/locked/private thread transitions and forum/media defaults do not lose fields or bypass permission checks.
Examples cover a forum post, thread history/member lifecycle and cache-free channel lookup.

workstreams.title: Complete messages, embeds, attachments and history
scope: Expand full/partial Message models for references, forwards/snapshots, interaction metadata, calls, system messages, flags, stickers, mentions, edits and deleted references.
Add history/cursor iterators, bulk deletion, current paginated pins, pin/unpin, publishing/crossposting and the documented guild-message search endpoint with access/availability handling.
Complete supported rich embed/attachment fields, suppressed notifications/embeds, scheduled delete, TTS and message flags without implying arbitrary outgoing fields are valid.
Add explicit file/stream/filesystem sources, spoiler/description/voice-message metadata, progress, cancellation and zero/low-copy multipart replay constraints.
Derive effective upload limits from current app/interaction/server context when available, keeping configurable library safety caps distinct from Discord platform limits.
Preserve omitted/null/clear edits, mention suppression, retained attachments and permission-sensitive fields across ordinary, webhook, interaction and V2 message operations.
Handle new/deprecated pin routes and other compatibility aliases deliberately, and keep message schemas ready for unknown fields/types.
acceptance: Message resource routes and public Message/PartialMessage/Attachment/Embed/File members are mapped to wrappers or explicit access/deprecation decisions.
History/pins/search pagination, bulk age restrictions, attachment retries and cancelled streamed uploads pass bounded-memory fixtures.
Payload equivalence tests verify text/embed/file/forward/ephemeral/V2 variants against the current reviewed schema.

workstreams.title: Reactions, emoji, stickers and expressive metadata
scope: Extend own reactions to user/all/emoji clearing and paginated reaction-user enumeration, including normal/burst reaction metadata and typed raw/cached events.
Add Unicode/partial/custom Emoji models, formatting, guild/application emoji CRUD, limits/assets and role/permission restrictions.
Add standard/guild stickers, packs/items, format/asset handling and supported create/edit/delete/send operations.
Preserve premium/availability flags, deleted emoji references, reaction count details and unknown expressive metadata.
acceptance: Encoded emoji paths, burst/normal counts, pagination, unavailable emoji and sticker formats have fixtures.
Application versus guild emoji ownership/auth and audit requirements are enforced per endpoint.
Unsupported formats or inaccessible media do not masquerade as successful sends/downloads.

workstreams.title: Polls and vote lifecycle
scope: Implement Poll/PollAnswer/media/layout models, creation, duration/multiple-choice settings and current send/edit restrictions.
Provide poll expiry/end operations, result/count interpretation and paginated voters for each answer.
Dispatch raw/cached vote add/remove events and preserve partial/unfinalized result semantics.
Integrate message, webhook and interaction payload support only where the current platform allows polls.
acceptance: Poll create/end/voter pagination and incomplete/final results match the current schema.
Deletion, uncached votes, timeout and permission failures are covered without assuming complete vote caches.
Poll helpers interact correctly with deferred interaction responses and incompatible V2 payload rules.

workstreams.title: Webhooks, webhook messages and HTTP event delivery
scope: Implement webhook create/list/fetch/edit/delete and execution with URL/token credentials, wait semantics, thread/forum targets and supported payload variants.
Provide WebhookMessage/partial target edit/delete/fetch helpers and safe shared attachment/embed/component support.

Expose an async webhook client independent of a Gateway Client; evaluate an explicit blocking adapter equivalent to SyncWebhook without blocking the event loop or claiming a Python-only API is already ported.
Treat outgoing Webhook Events separately from incoming webhook execution and interaction callbacks: verify signatures, acknowledge, deduplicate and handle retries/order semantics.
Parse application-authorized/deauthorized, entitlement, lobby and supported social message event envelopes according to access scope.
Protect webhook credentials in URLs/logs, bound request bodies and define replay/idempotency behavior for network uncertainty.
acceptance: Webhook execution, followup/original-response reuse and independent HTTP clients have auth-isolation and payload fixtures.
Event signature/PING/retry/duplicate/out-of-order cases are tested; no real event endpoint is required in PR CI.
Any blocking adapter is explicit, opt-in and guarded against event-loop use; unsupported modes remain documented decisions.

workstreams.title: Audit logs and Auto Moderation
scope: Implement audit-log async pagination, action/category enums, target/actor resolution, optional reasons and typed before/after diffs including unknown change keys.
Cover current action-specific diff fields, secondary entries, deleted targets, integration/webhook references and partial user/member state.
Implement AutoMod rule list/get/create/edit/delete with keyword/regex/preset/mention-spam triggers, exempt roles/channels and supported actions.
Add typed/raw rule create/update/delete and action-execution events with permission/intents and optional message-content handling.
Expose current rule limits and validation errors from reviewed schemas without promising that cached authorization is authoritative.
acceptance: Audit actions and AutoMod endpoint/event families are traceable to typed models and fixtures.
Unknown diffs, deleted actors/targets and unavailable content do not crash parsing or fabricate complete values.
Rule mutations preserve audit reasons, permission errors and regex/limit field-error details.

workstreams.title: Scheduled events and stage instances
scope: Implement scheduled-event create/fetch/list/edit/delete, entity types/privacy/status, recurrence/exceptions and external-location metadata where currently supported.
Support interested-user enumeration, event-user add/remove updates and invite/event associations with pagination.
Implement StageInstance CRUD, stage metadata, speaker/request-to-speak voice-state helpers and stage-specific permission rules.
Preserve optional dates, canceled/completed state and partial linked channel/member data.
acceptance: Schedule status transitions, recurring-event fields and interested-user pagination have time/permission fixtures.
Stage instance lifecycle and voice-state dependencies are tested separately from audio playback.
Current upstream schedule/stage fields and event families have explicit model mappings.

workstreams.title: Soundboard and voice effects
scope: Implement default/guild sound listing/fetch/create/edit/delete and sound assets, volume, emoji, availability and ownership metadata.
Support Gateway soundboard requests/chunks and sound create/update/delete events.
Add send-sound/voice-effect helpers with voice connection, external-sound permission and current source-guild requirements.
Model voice channel effect animation/sound metadata; do not mistake metadata events for implemented audio transport.
acceptance: Soundboard resource endpoints and public sound/effect model families have typed fixtures.
Playback-dependent operations stay unavailable until the voice handshake/encryption prerequisites in W28 are satisfied.
Missing permissions, unavailable sounds, partial caches and cross-guild requests fail explicitly.

workstreams.title: Applications, teams, OAuth2 and linked roles
scope: Implement AppInfo/partial info, teams/members/ownership, installation parameters, application flags and supported current application edits.
Add OAuth2 scope/permission URL builders, authorization-code/PKCE and client-credential adapters, refresh/revoke/expiry handling with injected credential storage.
Support guild/user installation contexts, account connections and approved OAuth-only operations with distinct bearer-grant capabilities.
Implement application role-connection metadata and per-user linked-role connection data, with localization and explicit grant requirements.
Cover discovery/verification/privacy-policy/terms configuration as documented prerequisites, not SDK-created approval or permissions.
Keep application identity/game-profile and Social SDK extensions explicitly tracked under W31 rather than silently omitting them.
acceptance: OAuth grant/expiry/revocation, install URLs and team/application payloads have synthetic contract fixtures.
Bot tokens, user grants and application credentials are never interchangeable or persisted by hidden defaults.
Public application/team/role-connection surfaces have typed mappings and documented platform prerequisites.

workstreams.title: SKUs, entitlements, subscriptions and purchases
scope: Implement SKU/entitlement/subscription models and supported list/fetch/test/create/delete/consume operations with cursor pagination.
Parse premium buttons, role subscriptions, purchase notifications and interaction entitlements without treating a cached entitlement as permanently valid access.
Support entitlement/subscription create/update/delete Gateway and webhook event envelopes and expiration/ownership semantics.
Provide test-entitlement examples and safe raw access while leaving billing, storefront rules and business authorization decisions to the application.
Track premium-app eligibility, regional/access restrictions and reviewed scopes explicitly; no account creation, purchase or automatic charge belongs in SDK initialization.
acceptance: Current commerce resource routes and public models/events have fixtures for expired, revoked, consumed and paginated states.
No live billing action runs in automated tests; examples use synthetic data or explicitly requested test entitlements.
Access failures and unknown future entitlement/subscription types remain representable.

workstreams.title: Voice transport, DAVE and audio sources
scope: Implement voice state/server handshakes, current voice Gateway version/opcodes, UDP discovery, RTP sequencing/timing, speaking state and reconnect/buffered resume.

Implement supported transport encryption and DAVE E2EE negotiation/transitions/MLS membership changes with reviewed maintained crypto dependencies such as Discord libdave; do not design custom cryptography.
Track DAVE binary frames, protocol-version changes, key epochs and secret cleanup; recheck the current mandatory-E2EE policy before claiming voice support.
Provide VoiceClient/VoiceProtocol extension points, move/connect/disconnect, latency/state and bounded playback queues.
Provide PCM/Opus AudioSource, encoding, streaming, volume and pause/resume/stop/after callbacks with strict event-loop isolation and pacing.
Offer optional FFmpeg process adapters with cancellation/cleanup, safe argument passing, dependency/license discovery and clear external-binary requirements.
Separate outgoing playback parity from voice receive, recording, video and screen-sharing proposals; those need explicit protocol/support/privacy scope review rather than an implied capability claim.
acceptance: No voice release is declared usable without current encryption/DAVE interoperability and reconnect/key-transition fixtures.
Audio timing, cancellation, subprocess cleanup, missing codecs and bounded buffers pass tests on supported platforms.
Optional audio/crypto dependencies do not enlarge the default message-only install without an explicit feature option.

workstreams.title: Sharding, multi-client operation and scale
scope: Provide manual and automatic shard managers, shard IDs/counts/info/events, per-shard lifecycle and multi-client isolation.
Coordinate identify concurrency/session-start quotas, reconnect storms and reshard/restart plans without assuming shared caches/process state.
Support pluggable coordination across processes as an optional adapter, with bounded dispatch/REST admission and explicit per-account/global limits.
Define executor/thread ownership, per-shard state routing, guild partitioning and error aggregation.
Run sustained-load, partial-outage and rolling-shutdown experiments with recorded queue, memory and latency distributions.
acceptance: Synthetic multi-shard failures do not exhaust identify budgets or leak tasks/queues across clients.
AutoShardedClient/Bot use cases have typed equivalents and per-shard observability without mandatory external infrastructure.
Large-bot benchmarks report workloads, caches, hardware, compiler and dependencies instead of universal speed claims.

workstreams.title: Advanced extension points, observability and performance
scope: Expose safe raw REST/Gateway, transport/middleware hooks, serializer/converter injection and executor access without requiring beginners to configure internals.
Add opt-in structured logging, metrics/tracing and error/queue/REST/heartbeat/cache diagnostics with stable names and comprehensive credential/content redaction.
Define memory/queue/allocator/worker budgets and an advanced configuration surface with conservative defaults and no global background telemetry.
Profile model/JSON copies, coroutine allocations, cooldown cleanup, multipart buffers and cache churn before adding pools, arenas, LTO or allocator hooks.
Expand paired benchmark scenarios to unknown commands, converters/checks, interaction serialization, V2 layouts, cache-free/cached events and streaming uploads.
Measure p50/p95/p99, throughput, CPU, RSS/peak/retained memory, idle work, build time and distribution size across static/shared and equivalent feature sets.
Separate real network/Discord limits from CPU work, retain raw data and establish regression thresholds on controlled runners rather than noisy shared CI timings.
acceptance: Instrumentation is bounded and opt-in, and does not reveal message bodies, bot/OAuth/webhook tokens or crypto keys by default.
Low-level customization preserves auth/rate-limit/cancellation invariants unless a separately documented unsafe boundary is deliberately selected.
Each optimization has a reproducible bottleneck, before/after evidence and correctness/ownership checks.

workstreams.title: Access-gated and adjacent platform surfaces
scope: Review Lobby REST, linked channels/messages and application identity/profile/game-stats endpoints individually for authentication, approval and product applicability; retain their route inventory even when not part of bot-core parity.
Track Social SDK provisional accounts, account merging/linking, friends/relationships, game invites and game voice as a separate integration scope, not as bot-token/self-bot functionality.
Track Embedded App SDK Activities, entry-point launch callbacks, activity purchases and browser/desktop bridges separately from the C++ bot runtime.
Review RPC, Certified Devices and desktop rich-presence surfaces for current authorization/deprecation and SDK ownership; do not promise unsupported user-account automation.
Track website component-embed/link-preview output as an optional website integration, distinct from outgoing bot embeds and Components V2 messages.
For every gated surface record supported credentials, approval restrictions, dependency/license costs, intended C++ adapter and a written included/deferred/out-of-scope decision with a reason.
Keep undocumented/private APIs, self-bots, token harvesting and platform approval bypasses outside supported bot-library scope.
acceptance: Every official index page outside normal bot-core APIs has a named scope decision; no adjacent surface disappears from the inventory without explanation.
Scope exclusions never masquerade as implemented discord.py parity or imply that raw requests bypass authorization.
Optional integrations are revisited when public bot applicability changes upstream, with explicit examples and access prerequisites.

workstreams.title: Builds, packaging, releases and supply chain
scope: Maintain Linux GCC/Clang, Windows MSVC/MinGW/UCRT static/shared consumers and add declared macOS/AppleClang/ARM64/libc++ coverage with explicit support levels.
Audit symbol exports, transitive dependencies, relocatable CMake/pkg-config installs, compiler/standard-library ABI policy and pre-1.0 runtime naming.
Keep optional voice/crypto/HTTP-server/telemetry adapters isolated; support dependency pinning, offline builds and a documented minimal install.
Continue version-to-immutable-tag-to-tested-assets-to-published-release automation, idempotent retries, checksums and source-only credential-safe packaging.
Add reproducibility/SBOM/provenance/signing decisions, dependency/license/CVE review and platform trust-store/runtime deployment checks.
Maintain project-hosted Conan/vcpkg/MSYS2 recipes and optional configured uploads; central registry acceptance remains a distinct reviewed submission, never a false availability claim.
Reduce duplicated expensive CI matrices for documentation/version workflows while retaining source/schema checks and frozen-tag retry compatibility.
acceptance: Every declared compiler/platform/package combination has a relocated installed consumer and version/dependency check.
Publication cannot silently stop at a tag, overwrite an immutable release or upload unrelated dependencies/secrets.
Optional integrations have independently testable package features and complete third-party notices.

workstreams.title: Compatibility, security and adversarial verification
scope: Maintain unit, local REST/Gateway, installed-consumer and static/shared tests plus sanitizer and leak/cancellation checks for each new feature family.
Add property/fuzz tests for JSON, command parsing, component/modal trees, signatures, compression, multipart streams and unknown enum/permission values.
Add fault injection for packet loss, stalled transfers, out-of-order/duplicate events, 429 remaps, response uncertainty, deadlines and resource exhaustion.
Build contract/payload fixtures from the reviewed protocol, distinguish application safety caps from Discord limits and document deprecated/removed endpoint handling.
Keep real credentials, live purchases and destructive account/server actions out of CI; define an owner-run opt-in authenticated smoke suite for currently shipped capabilities.
Review URL/download policies, signed HTTP ingress, sensitive logs, dependency vulnerabilities, audit reasons and least-privilege operation requirements.
Track API/source/ABI compatibility and migration examples; a planned item is complete only after implementation, documentation and appropriate tests exist.
acceptance: Every completed feature points to executable evidence and a test covering its non-happy-path lifecycle; no broad raw-JSON test is used to claim typed feature coverage.
Security/cancellation/bounded-memory regressions block publication; unstable external mirrors are retried without removing checks.
Live-platform validation is reported only when explicitly executed with the owner's authorization.

workstreams.title: Developer ergonomics, reference and examples
scope: Provide minimal function-based and subclass/Cog examples for each shipped feature, then realistic prefix/slash/context-menu/View/LayoutView/modal/task/voice compositions.
Prefer owning values, coherent naming/options/builders and clear compiler diagnostics; avoid mandatory raw JSON, lifetime tricks or excessive boilerplate for ordinary bots.
Publish reference/cookbook, setup/intents/permission guidance, custom help/error hooks, localization, cancellation, extension and performance recipes.
Maintain an honest discord.py mapping with full/partial/planned/access-gated statuses, known differences and explicit unsupported behavior.
Add migration guides for each minor/API change and document how Python constructs map to C++ concepts without pretending decorators/modules/GC have identical semantics.
Review tutorial snippets as compiled examples where practical and test package installation from clean, relocated environments.
Collect usability review against concrete developer tasks and include advanced escape-hatch examples without exposing implementation noise in the basic API.
acceptance: An ordinary developer can follow a documented example for each advertised feature without unmentioned manual REST or ownership machinery.
Documentation and examples use APIs that actually compile for the advertised version and identify partial support clearly.
The feature-comparison page never claims complete parity from a broad roadmap heading or raw transport access.

workstreams.title: Coverage registry and upstream-change review
scope: Maintain dated official Discord resource/section/route/component and discord.py documented-symbol inventories, with source URLs, body hashes and a pinned C++ audit commit.
Map every captured page, public API root and component type to a named workstream; retain explicit reasons for gated/adjacent surfaces.
Keep roadmap anchors, dependencies, acceptance criteria, evidence paths and the Mermaid view consistent; reject unmapped items and dependency cycles.
Run the offline registry audit in source CI and add focused tests for missing mappings, new components, cycles and misleading completion/status evidence.

Before each feature-family implementation/release, run the explicit upstream comparison; review new methods, fields, permissions, opcodes, deprecations and changelog entries before updating the snapshot.
Require implementation plus serialization/behavior/cancellation/error/permission examples and tests before promoting a capability; track deferred work rather than deleting it.
Document that mapped/reviewed inventory counts are planning coverage, not implemented-feature percentages or a guarantee against future upstream changes.
acceptance: The checked-in inventory has zero unmapped captured pages/API roots/component types and all workstream dependencies form a DAG.
Unreviewed additions/removals or changed upstream source content are reported and fail the explicit online audit until reviewed deliberately.
A future maintainer can reproduce source collection and inspect exact mapping decisions without asking the user to enumerate missing features.
